title: How do we add two numbers on the abacus?
description: Two numbers are set on either side of the abacus board and their counters are brought together, line by line. Counters are regrouped when a line holds ten. Keeko's doubt is that ten counters can stay on the ones line.
teaching_notes: One idea: bring the counters of each line together, then ten on a line become one on the next line up. Watch for students who leave ten counters on a line.

source: Add 2907 and 43 on the counting board.
video_script.why: The child adds on the book's abacus by bringing counters together and regrouping ten on a line into one on the next line.
video_script.substitution: Bring together the counters of each line, then swap ten counters on a line for one counter on the next line up.
video_script.anchor: the book's abacus: lines for one, ten, a hundred and a thousand, with a counter above a line worth five
video_script.wrong_answer: leave ten counters on the ones line
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko leaves ten counters on the ones line; a line never holds ten, so ten ones become one counter on the tens line
video_script.payoff_line: The board shows two thousand nine hundred fifty.
maths_rules: 2907: thousands 2; hundreds 9 = one above (5) + 4 on the line; tens 0; ones 7 = one above (5) + 2 on the line
ones: 7 + 3 = 10, so ten ones become 1 counter on the tens line
tens: 4 + 1 = 5, shown by one counter above the tens line
hundreds 9 and thousands 2 stay the same; the board reads 2 thousands, 9 hundreds, 5 tens and 0 ones = 2950
video_script.design: One idea: ten on a line become one on the next line up. The abacus lines stay on the board while the counters move.

<bookmark mark='board'/>The two numbers are placed on either side of the board.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We must add two thousand nine hundred seven and forty three. What number will the board show?

narration: <bookmark mark='lines'/>Each line of the abacus stands for a power of ten, starting from one.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Counters on a line show how many of that landmark a number has.
<bookmark mark='five'/>A counter above a line is worth five.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, two thousand nine hundred seven on one side, and forty three on the other.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sum on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the sum, shown by counters on one side.

beats.on_screen: 2907: 2 on the thousands line; 9 on the hundreds line as one above and 4 on it; none on tens; 7 on ones as one above and 2 on it. 43: 4 on tens, 3 on ones

marks.left: the counters of 2907 are shown on the left
marks.right: the counters of 43 are shown on the right

narration: <bookmark mark='left'/>Step one, read the counters. Two thousand nine hundred seven has two on the thousands line. <bookmark mark='hund'/>Hundreds are nine, which is one above the line and four on it.
<bookmark mark='right'/>It has none on the tens line, and seven ones. Forty three has four tens and three ones.

beats.on_screen: ones: 7 + 3 = 10, so ten ones become 1 counter on the tens line

marks.ones: the counters on the ones line come together
marks.ten: 7 + 3 = 10 is written and the ten ones are replaced by 1 counter on the tens line

narration: <bookmark mark='ones'/>Step two, bring the counters of the ones line together. Seven ones and three ones make ten ones.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>A line cannot hold ten, so the ten ones become one counter on the tens line.

beats.on_screen: tens: 4 + 1 = 5, shown by one counter above the tens line

marks.tens: 4 + 1 = 5 is written for the tens line
marks.above: the five counters become one counter above the tens line

narration: <bookmark mark='tens'/>Step three, bring the tens together. We had four tens, and one more arrived, so there are five.
<bookmark mark='above'/>Five on a line are shown by one counter above the line.

beats.on_screen: hundreds 9 and thousands 2 stay; read: 2 thousands, 9 hundreds, 5 tens, 0 ones; check: 2907 + 40 = 2947, then 3 more

marks.read: the board is read line by line from the thousands down
marks.check: 2907 + 40 = 2947 is written, and 3 more is ticked against the board

narration: <bookmark mark='read'/>Step four, read the board. The hundreds and thousands did not change. We have two thousands, nine hundreds, five tens and no ones.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Check by adding in steps. Two thousand nine hundred seven plus forty is two thousand nine hundred forty seven. Three more gives the total on the board.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The board shows two thousand nine hundred fifty.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's ones line crowded with ten counters; the ten counters slide into one counter on the tens line

marks.doubt: ten counters appear on the ones line
marks.slide: the ten counters slide into one counter on the tens line

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks we can leave ten counters on the ones line, since seven and three make ten.
<bookmark mark='slide'/>But ten ones are worth exactly one ten. A line never holds ten, so the ten counters become one counter on the line above.
